name: What Should Be in a Garage Addition Contract?

mainEntity.name: What should be included in a garage addition contract before work starts?
mainEntity.text: What should be included in a garage addition contract before work starts?

acceptedAnswer.text: A complete contract protects both the homeowner and the contractor by setting expectations before construction begins. For a garage addition, the agreement should describe the exact structure, dimensions, materials, finishes, site work, utility work, and who is responsible for permits and inspections. It should also explain the payment schedule, how change orders are approved, what happens if site conditions differ from the estimate, and which warranties apply to labor and materials. In Los Angeles County, it is especially useful to confirm whether the contractor is handling engineering coordination, energy compliance items, and city-specific permit steps. Homeowners should avoid vague contracts that simply say “build garage addition” without itemizing the scope. The clearer the contract, the easier it is to prevent budget surprises, schedule disputes, and confusion over unfinished items at the end of the job.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage addition contract should include the full scope of work, payment schedule, start and finish targets, permit responsibilities, change-order process, material allowances, warranties, and cleanup expectations. It should also clearly state what is excluded so there are fewer disputes during construction.
